{"metadata":{"description":"Hash-anchored read/edit/grep tools for DeepSeek Harness: every line carries a content hash, stale anchors are rejected before touching the file.","id":"gh:1333756247","install_available":false,"language":"TypeScript","name":"dsh-tool-hashline","slug":"InklingYoshi584/dsh-tool-hashline","topics":["dsh-plugin","hashline"]},"paragraphs":[{"id":"p1s1","text":"Hash-anchored read/edit/grep tools for DeepSeek Harness: every line carries a content hash, stale an"},{"id":"p1s2","text":"chors are rejected before touching the file."},{"id":"p2s1","text":"# dsh-tool-hashline"},{"id":"p3s1","text":"Hash-anchored `read`, `edit`, and `grep` tools for DeepSeek Harness (DSH). Stale anchors fail the whole call — never relocated, never fuzz"},{"id":"p3s4","text":"y-matched, never silently applied to the wrong line."},{"id":"p4s1","text":"Protocol adopted from pi-hashline-edit (MIT), inspired by oh-my-pi."},{"id":"p5s1","text":"## How to install"},{"id":"p6s1","text":"### Prerequisites"},{"id":"p7s1","text":"- **Node.js ≥ 20** (for running dsh and the plugin).

- No install: `"},{"id":"p7s2","text":"npx @deepseek-ai/dsh <command>` — note the bare command always needs a profile: `npx @deepseek-ai/ds"},{"id":"p7s3","text":"h web` or `npx @deepseek-ai/dsh --profile headless "task"`.
- Global install (gives you the bare `ds"},{"id":"p7s4","text":"h` command on PATH, plus pnpm in one go): `npm i -g pnpm @deepseek-ai/dsh`.
- **pnpm** — the `dsh pl"},{"id":"p7s5","text":"ugin` command forwards to it (installed by the global command above).
- A **DeepSeek API key** for l"},{"id":"p7s6","text":"ive sessions (configure it in the Web UI at Settings → Models, or export `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`)."},{"id":"p8s1","text":"### Step 1 — get the plugin"},{"id":"p9s1","text":"**Option A: npm (recommended)** — published on the registry, installs the prebuilt `lib/` bundle:"},{"id":"p10s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p11s1","text":"**Option B: from source** (development):"},{"id":"p12s1","text":"[代码示例省略，未执行]"},{"id":"p13s1","text":"The `@deepseek-ai/*` harness packages are dev dependencies here on purpose: at runtime the plugin re"},{"id":"p13s2","text":"solves them from the dsh installation through the profile's maintained flat fallback (`$DSH_HOME/pro"},{"id":"p13s3","text":"files/node_modules` symlinks), so no duplicate harness core ever ships with the plugin. `npm install"},{"id":"p13s4","text":"` only needs to succeed for the tests; running the plugin needs nothing but the preset row."},{"id":"p14s1","text":"### Step 2 — author the `hashline` preset"},{"id":"p15s1","text":"The plugin replaces the stock tools by **preset-plane shadowing**: a preset that mounts this plugin "},{"id":"p15s2","text":"instead of `tool-fs` gives its sessions the hashline `read`/`edit`/`grep` while everything else keep"},{"id":"p15s3","text":"s working from the host composition. Settings → Agent presets should show **"In use: Hashline"**."},{"id":"p27s1","text":"### What the swap changes"},{"id":"p28s1","text":"On the `hashline` preset, `read`/`edit` (and `grep` when enabled) are the hashline versions — the pr"},{"id":"p28s2","text":"eset's scope layer shadows the global `tool-fs`/`tool-fs-search` tools **by name**. `write`, `read_i"},{"id":"p28s3","text":"mage`, `glob`, `bash`, and everything else keep working from the host composition, and subagents inh"},{"id":"p28s4","text":"bash`, and everything else keep working from the host composition, and subagents inherit the preset."},{"id":"p29s1","text":"### Headless / no-roster deployments"},{"id":"p30s1","text":"The `headless` profile composes no preset roster. Two things can be true at edit time:"},{"id":"p34s2","text":" the file changed since the read (a concurrent write, a drift, an earlier edit in the same turn), an"},{"id":"p34s3","text":"d the quoted text appears in more than one place. Stock edit tools handle this badly:"},{"id":"p35s1","text":"- **Literal string-replace** (`old_string`/`new_string`, what DSH ships) requires the quoted text to"},{"id":"p35s2","text":" match *exactly once*. Any drift means a retry loop; ambiguity means "make it more specific" busywor"},{"id":"p35s3","text":"k.
- **Line-number editing** is worse: numbers silently point at the *wrong* line after any shift, a"},{"id":"p35s4","text":"nd the edit corrupts code the model never looked at.
- The problem is real enough that Cursor traine"},{"id":"p35s5","text":"d a dedicated 70B model just to apply edits correctly."},{"id":"p36s1","text":"The evidence that the harness — not the model — is the lever: Can Balioglu's benchmark kept 15 model"},{"id":"p36s2","text":"s fixed and swapped only the edit format. Hashline beat patch for 14 of 16 configurations, **and the"},{"id":"p36s3","text":" weakest models gained the most**. Better anchoring rescues the long tail of models you'd otherwise "},{"id":"p36s4","text":"dels gained the most**. Better anchoring rescues the long tail of models you'd otherwise give up on."},{"id":"p37s1","text":"What hashline changes:"},{"id":"p38s1","text":"| Property | Stock `edit` | hashline |"},{"id":"p39s1","text":"| Anchor | literal `old_string` text | `LINE#HASH` content hash |
| File drifted since read | error,"},{"id":"p39s2","text":" retry with new text | error **naming the stale anchor**, re-read, retry |
| Same line text appears "},{"id":"p39s3","text":"twice | ambiguity, "be more specific" | context hashing makes collisions rare; ambiguity lists candi"},{"id":"p39s4","text":"dates |
| Multiple hunks | one call per hunk | **N ops in one call**, one snapshot, one atomic write"},{"id":"p39s5","text":" |
| After an edit | re-read the file | fresh `--- Anchors ---` block → chained edits with no re-rea"},{"id":"p39s6","text":"d |
| Search-to-edit | grep, then open, then quote | `grep` returns the same anchors → edit with no "},{"id":"p39s7","text":"to-edit | grep, then open, then quote | `grep` returns the same anchors → edit with no read at all |"},{"id":"p40s1","text":"On top of that, DSH's own observation policy stays in force: read-before-write and a file-level vers"},{"id":"p40s2","text":"ion CAS still guard the whole file, while the anchors guard the *lines*. You get line-level correctn"},{"id":"p40s3","text":"ess and file-level freshness together."}],"truncated":true}
